hotlines.name: NYC Well
hotlines.organization: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene / Mayor's Office of Community Mental Health
hotlines.target: NYC residents in emotional distress or mental health/substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: Distinct from national 988; also branded as NYC988. Text WELL to 65173.

hotlines.name: NYC HOPE Hotline
hotlines.organization: NYC Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
hotlines.target: NYC residents experiencing domestic or intimate partner violence
hotlines.notes: Also known as 1-800-621-HOPE; TTY 1-866-604-5350. Run by the city, distinct from the NY State DV/SA coalition hotline.

hotlines.name: LA County Department of Mental Health Help Line
hotlines.organization: Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health
hotlines.target: LA County residents needing mental health or substance use crisis support
hotlines.notes: Press 1 for crisis/mental health, press 2 for substance use, press 3 for veteran/military family support.

hotlines.name: 211 LA County
hotlines.organization: 211 LA County
hotlines.target: LA County residents seeking health and human services referrals
hotlines.notes: California has no single unified statewide 211 number; 211 LA County operates its own distinct toll-free line (1-800-339-6993) for callers outside the county.

hotlines.name: LA County Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: Los Angeles County Department of Public Health
hotlines.target: LA County residents experiencing domestic violence
hotlines.notes: County-run hotline, distinct from the California statewide DV coalition hotline.

hotlines.name: NAMI Chicago Helpline
hotlines.organization: NAMI Chicago (in partnership with Cook County Health)
hotlines.target: Chicago and suburban Cook County residents seeking mental health support/referrals
hotlines.notes: Also known as 833-NAMI-CHI. Sustained via multi-year investment from Cook County Health's Office of Behavioral Health; not 24/7.

hotlines.name: 211 Metro Chicago
hotlines.organization: United Way of Metro Chicago (in partnership with the City of Chicago and Cook County)
hotlines.target: Cook County residents seeking human/social services referrals
hotlines.notes: Localized service for Cook County, distinct from the statewide 211 Illinois network operated by the Illinois Department of Human Services.

hotlines.name: Chicago Domestic Violence Help Line
hotlines.organization: City of Chicago Department of Family and Support Services / Chicago Metropolitan Battered Women's Network
hotlines.target: Chicago residents experiencing domestic violence
hotlines.notes: City-run since 1998, distinct from the statewide Illinois Domestic Violence Hotline operated by The Network.

hotlines.name: The Harris Center Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: The Harris Center for Mental Health and IDD
hotlines.target: Harris County residents in a mental health or IDD crisis
hotlines.notes: The Harris Center is Harris County's designated Local Mental Health Authority; select option 1 for crisis line. Distinct from 988 and Texas statewide numbers.

hotlines.name: HAWC Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: Houston Area Women's Center (HAWC)
hotlines.target: Harris County/Houston-area residents experiencing domestic violence
hotlines.notes: HAWC is designated as Harris County's primary domestic violence service provider, listed on the county's official Domestic Violence Resources page; distinct from the National DV Hotline.

hotlines.name: Maricopa County (Central Arizona) Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Solari Crisis & Human Services
hotlines.target: Maricopa County (Central Arizona region) residents in a behavioral health crisis
hotlines.notes: Arizona is divided into regional crisis lines (Northern/Central/Southern); this is the Central Arizona line covering Maricopa County specifically, operated by Solari under contract with the region's behavioral health system, distinct from a single unified statewide number.

hotlines.name: Maricopa County Domestic Violence Hotline (A New Leaf)
hotlines.organization: A New Leaf
hotlines.target: Maricopa County residents experiencing domestic violence
hotlines.notes: Also listed as 1-844-SAFEDVS. Distinct from the Arizona Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence (ACESDV) statewide helpline (1-800-782-6400).

hotlines.name: Philadelphia Crisis Line (DBHIDS)
hotlines.organization: City of Philadelphia Department of Behavioral Health and Intellectual disAbility Services (DBHIDS)
hotlines.target: Philadelphia residents experiencing a behavioral health emergency
hotlines.notes: Dispatches Mobile Crisis Teams; distinct from 988 and run directly by the city.

hotlines.name: Philadelphia Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: Women Against Abuse (with Congreso de Latinos Unidos, Lutheran Settlement House, Women In Transition), supported by the City of Philadelphia Office of Domestic Violence Strategies
hotlines.target: Philadelphia residents experiencing intimate partner/domestic violence
hotlines.notes: City-wide point of access since 2005, run by a consortium of local providers with city support; distinct from the Pennsylvania statewide DV coalition hotline.

hotlines.name: CHCS 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Center for Health Care Services (CHCS) - Bexar County's Local Mental Health Authority
hotlines.target: Bexar County residents experiencing a mental health, substance use, or emotional crisis
hotlines.notes: Operated by CHCS, the county-designated Local Mental Health Authority; listed as a county crisis resource on the official Bexar County Behavioral Health page.

hotlines.name: Family Violence Prevention Services 24-Hour Hotline
hotlines.organization: Family Violence Prevention Services, Inc. (The Battered Women & Children's Shelter)
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in San Antonio and Bexar County
hotlines.notes: Locally operated 45+ year shelter and crisis line serving Bexar County; distinct from the statewide/national domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: San Diego Access and Crisis Line (ACL)
hotlines.organization: County of San Diego Health and Human Services Agency (Behavioral Health Services), operated via Optum
hotlines.target: San Diego County residents in mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: County-run crisis line distinct from 988; also used to dispatch the county's Mobile Crisis Response Teams (MCRT).

hotlines.name: Center for Community Solutions 24/7 Crisis Hotline
hotlines.organization: Center for Community Solutions
hotlines.target: victims of relationship violence and sexual assault in San Diego County
hotlines.notes: Locally operated San Diego County crisis hotline for domestic violence and sexual assault, also listed on the County's official One Safe Place Family Justice Center resource page; distinct from the national/state DV hotline.

hotlines.name: NTBHA Mental Health Crisis Hotline
hotlines.organization: North Texas Behavioral Health Authority (NTBHA)
hotlines.target: residents of Dallas County (and Ellis, Hunt, Kaufman, Navarro, Rockwall counties) in a mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: NTBHA is Dallas County's designated Local Mental Health Authority; line dispatches the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team (MCOT) and also feeds the RIGHT Care police co-response program. Distinct from 988.

hotlines.name: Genesis 24-Hour Helpline
hotlines.organization: Genesis Women's Shelter & Support
hotlines.target: women and children experiencing domestic violence in the Dallas area
hotlines.notes: Locally operated Dallas domestic violence shelter and helpline (call or text), distinct from the state/national domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: Integral Care 24/7 Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Integral Care (Austin-Travis County's Local Mental Health Authority)
hotlines.target: Travis County residents in a mental health, substance use, or IDD crisis
hotlines.notes: Integral Care is the official mental health authority for Austin-Travis County and also hosts the local 988 call center; this local crisis line is distinct and provides phone, text, and chat crisis intervention plus Mobile Crisis Outreach Team dispatch.

hotlines.name: SAFEline
hotlines.organization: The SAFE Alliance
hotlines.target: survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, and human trafficking in Travis County
hotlines.notes: SAFE Alliance (merger of Austin Children's Shelter and SafePlace) runs Austin/Travis County's local DV/SA hotline, chatline, and textline; distinct from the statewide/national hotline.

hotlines.name: Behavioral Health Services Call Center
hotlines.organization: County of Santa Clara Behavioral Health Services Department
hotlines.target: Santa Clara County residents in a mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.geography: San Jose / Santa Clara County, California
hotlines.notes: County-run call center; residents with 408, 650, or 669 area codes are also routed here via 988, but this toll-free number is the county's direct line and works from any area code.

hotlines.name: TRUST Direct Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Santa Clara County Behavioral Health Services / Trusted Response Urgent Support Team (TRUST)
hotlines.target: residents of San Jose/Santa Clara County wanting a non-police mental health crisis response
hotlines.geography: San Jose / Santa Clara County, California
hotlines.notes: Direct line to Santa Clara County's TRUST program, a non-law-enforcement mobile crisis response team; created by the County Board of Supervisors as an alternative routing to 988 so callers can specifically request a non-police response.

hotlines.name: Next Door Solutions 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Next Door Solutions to Domestic Violence
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in San Jose and Santa Clara County
hotlines.geography: San Jose / Santa Clara County, California
hotlines.notes: Locally operated Santa Clara County domestic violence agency crisis line, distinct from the statewide/national DV hotline.

hotlines.name: MHMR of Tarrant County I-CARE Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: My Health My Resources (MHMR) of Tarrant County
hotlines.target: Tarrant County residents in a mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: MHMR is Tarrant County's designated Local Mental Health Authority; operates the I-CARE Call Center and dispatches the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team. TTY/TDD available at 817-569-4488. Distinct from 988.

hotlines.name: The Archway 24-Hour Hotline (formerly SafeHaven of Tarrant County)
hotlines.organization: The Archway
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in Fort Worth and Tarrant County
hotlines.notes: The organization rebranded from SafeHaven of Tarrant County to The Archway in 2025 but kept the same hotline number; it is described as the only dedicated domestic violence hotline for Tarrant County, distinct from the statewide/national hotline.

hotlines.name: 211 Northeast Florida (First Call for Help)
hotlines.organization: United Way of Northeast Florida
hotlines.target: Jacksonville/Duval County residents needing crisis and community resource referrals
hotlines.notes: Local 10-digit number for 211 Northeast Florida, distinct from a generic statewide 211 dial-in; also handles crisis calls and text 'Hello' to 211904.

hotlines.name: Hubbard House Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: Hubbard House, Inc.
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in Jacksonville/Duval County
hotlines.notes: Locally operated Duval County domestic violence shelter/hotline provider, distinct from the statewide Florida Domestic Violence Hotline.

hotlines.name: Netcare Access Crisis Hotline
hotlines.organization: Netcare Access / ADAMH Board of Franklin County
hotlines.target: Franklin County residents in mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: Also written as 614-276-CARE / 888-276-CARE. Netcare Access provides crisis intervention, stabilization and assessment for all Franklin County residents, funded/overseen by the ADAMH Board of Franklin County (Ohio's county behavioral health authority).

hotlines.name: 211 Central Ohio
hotlines.organization: LSS 211 Central Ohio (Lutheran Social Services)
hotlines.target: Franklin County residents needing referrals to local programs
hotlines.notes: Distinct local 10-digit number for 211 Central Ohio serving Franklin County, not just generic 211 dialing.

hotlines.name: Franklin County Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: The Center for Family Safety and Healing (Nationwide Children's Hospital)
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in Franklin County
hotlines.notes: Also written as 614-224-HOME. Long-running county-specific domestic violence hotline (formerly run by LSS CHOICES); operations transitioned to The Center for Family Safety and Healing in March 2026, same number retained. Distinct from Ohio's statewide domestic violence network.

hotlines.name: Mecklenburg County Mobile Crisis Team
hotlines.organization: The Affiliated Santé Group
hotlines.target: Mecklenburg County residents in behavioral/mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: Select option 1 for the Mobile Crisis Team. Free crisis intervention service for Mecklenburg County residents; also listed as an emergency contact on Mecklenburg County's Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) government site (cit.mecknc.gov/emergency-contacts).

hotlines.name: Greater Charlotte Hope Line
hotlines.organization: Safe Alliance
hotlines.target: domestic violence and sexual assault victims/survivors in Mecklenburg County
hotlines.notes: Locally run by Safe Alliance for Mecklenburg County residents, distinct from the North Carolina statewide domestic violence hotline. Live chat available weekdays 7am-11pm.

hotlines.name: Sandra Eskenazi Mental Health Center Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Eskenazi Health (Health & Hospital Corporation of Marion County)
hotlines.target: Marion County residents in mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: Crisis Intervention Unit and Mobile Crisis Recovery Team operated by Eskenazi Health, which is part of the Health & Hospital Corporation of Marion County, a county governmental entity.

hotlines.name: The Julian Center 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: The Julian Center
hotlines.target: domestic violence and sexual assault victims/survivors in Marion County
hotlines.notes: Marion County's largest domestic violence service provider; hotline is locally operated and distinct from any statewide Indiana domestic violence coalition line.

hotlines.name: SF Behavioral Health Access Line
hotlines.organization: San Francisco Department of Public Health
hotlines.target: San Francisco residents seeking mental health or substance use crisis support and services
hotlines.notes: TTY: 711. City/county-run access and crisis line distinct from 988, connecting callers to same-day/48-hour behavioral health services and the Behavioral Health Access Center.

hotlines.name: La Casa de las Madres 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: La Casa de las Madres
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in San Francisco
hotlines.notes: San Francisco-based domestic violence crisis line and shelter provider, works closely with SFPD; separate teen line at 877-923-0700. Distinct from the California statewide domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: King County Regional Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Crisis Connections (contracted by King County)
hotlines.target: King County residents in emotional/behavioral health crisis, can dispatch mobile crisis teams
hotlines.notes: King County recommends residents still use this Regional Crisis Line (in addition to 988) for local mobile crisis team dispatch; listed on official King County government crisis services page.

hotlines.name: DV Hopeline
hotlines.organization: New Beginnings
hotlines.target: domestic violence victims/survivors in Seattle/King County
hotlines.notes: Seattle's largest and oldest domestic violence service provider; hotline is locally run and distinct from the Washington State domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: STAR (Support Team Assisted Response) Program
hotlines.organization: City and County of Denver - Department of Public Health & Environment (Community Behavioral Health), staffed with WellPower clinicians and Denver Health paramedics
hotlines.hours: 7 days a week, 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. (911 dispatches STAR outside those hours to other response options)
hotlines.target: Denver residents experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis that is not life-threatening
hotlines.notes: City-run mobile co-responder alternative to police for behavioral health crises; a two-person van team (behavioral health clinician + paramedic/EMT) can be requested directly at this number or via the non-emergency line 720-913-2000, distinct from 988 and Colorado Crisis Services (844-493-8255).

hotlines.name: SafeHouse Denver 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: SafeHouse Denver
hotlines.target: domestic violence survivors and their children in the Denver area
hotlines.notes: Locally-run Denver domestic violence crisis line and shelter provider, distinct from Colorado's statewide DV coalition hotline.

hotlines.name: BEST (Boston Emergency Services Team)
hotlines.organization: Boston Medical Center / Boston Emergency Services Team (Boston's designated Emergency Services Program)
hotlines.target: individuals in the city of Boston experiencing a psychiatric or behavioral health crisis
hotlines.notes: Boston's contracted Emergency Services Program call center providing triage, mobile crisis response, and referrals; distinct from 988 and other regional Massachusetts ESPs.

hotlines.name: Mental Health Cooperative Mobile Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Mental Health Cooperative (Metro Nashville/Davidson County's designated crisis services provider)
hotlines.target: residents of Nashville/Davidson County experiencing a mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: Listed by the Metro Public Health Department as the local mobile crisis contact, distinct from 988 and the statewide Tennessee crisis lines.

hotlines.name: Family Safety Center (Office of Family Safety)
hotlines.organization: Metropolitan Government of Nashville & Davidson County, Office of Family Safety
hotlines.hours: 24/7 for emergency order-of-protection assistance; walk-in advocate services Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-6 p.m.
hotlines.target: victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, and other interpersonal violence in Davidson County
hotlines.notes: Metro government-run family justice center and crisis-intervention line, distinct from the Tennessee statewide domestic violence hotline (1-800-356-6767).

hotlines.name: DWIHN Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network (DWIHN), Wayne County's Community Mental Health Authority
hotlines.target: Wayne County residents experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis
hotlines.notes: County community mental health authority's crisis/access line; also operates the walk-in DWIHN 707 Crisis Care Center (313-833-3232). Distinct from 988 and Michigan's statewide lines.

hotlines.name: First Step 24-Hour Helpline
hotlines.organization: First Step (Wayne County's Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Comprehensive Agency)
hotlines.target: survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Wayne County
hotlines.notes: Designated comprehensive domestic and sexual violence agency serving Wayne County specifically, distinct from Michigan's statewide domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: Multnomah County Mental Health Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Multnomah County Behavioral Health Division
hotlines.target: residents of Multnomah County experiencing a mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: County-run crisis line distinct from 988, staffed 24/7 with interpretation services.

hotlines.name: Portland Street Response
hotlines.organization: City of Portland (Portland Fire & Rescue / Public Safety Service Area)
hotlines.target: people in Portland experiencing a mental health, behavioral health, or unsheltered crisis in public spaces
hotlines.notes: City-run non-police mobile crisis/outreach team; can be requested directly at this number or via 911. Distinct from the Multnomah County phone crisis line.

hotlines.name: Mobile Crisis Response Team (Southern Nevada)
hotlines.organization: Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health, Southern Nevada/Clark County region
hotlines.target: youth under 18 and their families in Clark County experiencing a behavioral or mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: Regionally-dedicated Southern Nevada/Clark County number (separate from other Nevada regions' Mobile Crisis Response Team lines) providing in-person crisis response for families; distinct from 988 and the statewide Nevada suicide/crisis lines.

hotlines.name: SafeNest 24/7 Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: SafeNest (Temporary Assistance for Domestic Crisis, Inc.)
hotlines.target: domestic violence survivors in Clark County
hotlines.notes: Clark County's primary domestic violence crisis hotline; SafeNest operates a separate rural-Nevada hotline (800-486-7282), and this number is distinct from the Nevada Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence's statewide line.

hotlines.name: Resiliency & Justice Center (formerly Vegas Strong Resiliency Center)
hotlines.organization: Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada, in partnership with Clark County and the City of Las Vegas
hotlines.target: victims of violent crime and mass-casualty events in the Las Vegas/Clark County area seeking trauma support, peer support, and free legal services
hotlines.notes: Originally launched as the Vegas Strong Resiliency Center after the October 1, 2017 mass shooting to serve Clark County/Las Vegas victims specifically; now the Resiliency & Justice Center, still locally operated and distinct from national or statewide crisis lines.

hotlines.name: Alliance Healthcare Services Adult Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Alliance Healthcare Services
hotlines.target: Adults in Shelby County experiencing a behavioral health crisis
hotlines.notes: Operated by Alliance Healthcare Services, the primary contracted behavioral health crisis provider for Shelby County; offers crisis assessment, mobile intervention and stabilization, distinct from 988. No one is turned away for inability to pay.

hotlines.name: Memphis Crisis Center
hotlines.organization: Memphis Crisis Center
hotlines.target: Residents of Memphis and the Mid-South experiencing emotional or suicidal crisis
hotlines.notes: Locally operated nonprofit crisis line running continuously since 1970; serves as Shelby County's designated local call center within the 988 network but retains its own long-standing local number and volunteer-staffed service.

hotlines.name: LINC 211 Memphis
hotlines.organization: Memphis Public Libraries (City of Memphis)
hotlines.target: Memphis/Shelby County residents seeking social-service referrals
hotlines.notes: City-run community-information line operated by Memphis Public Libraries with United Way of the Mid-South, with its own direct-dial numbers distinct from the generic statewide 211 short code. Limited hours, not a 24/7 crisis line.

hotlines.name: Family Safety Center 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Family Safety Center of Memphis and Shelby County
hotlines.target: Domestic violence victims/survivors in Memphis and Shelby County
hotlines.notes: Locally operated family justice center serving Memphis and Shelby County; distinct from the Tennessee statewide domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: Seven Counties Services Adult Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Seven Counties Services
hotlines.target: Jefferson County/Louisville Metro residents experiencing a behavioral health crisis
hotlines.notes: Seven Counties Services is the designated community mental health center for Jefferson County; this line is also used to trigger mobile crisis response and Louisville Metro's Crisis Call Diversion (Deflection) program.

hotlines.name: Center for Women and Families 24-Hour Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: The Center for Women and Families
hotlines.target: Survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Jefferson County and the surrounding region
hotlines.notes: Locally operated crisis line based in Louisville, distinct from Kentucky's statewide domestic violence coalition hotline; also covers Bullitt, Henry, Oldham, Shelby, Spencer and Trimble counties in KY plus Clark and Floyd counties in IN.

hotlines.name: Louisville Metro Crisis Call Diversion (Deflection)
hotlines.organization: Louisville Metro Government / LMPD, with Seven Counties Services
hotlines.target: Louisville residents in a mental/behavioral health crisis who want a non-police response
hotlines.notes: Accessed via 911 (request 'deflection response') or the LMPD non-emergency line 502-574-7111, option 5. Routes non-emergency mental-health-related 911 calls to trained Crisis Triage Workers instead of a police officer; expanded to all 8 LMPD divisions 24/7.

hotlines.name: Milwaukee County Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Milwaukee County Behavioral Health Services / Mental Health Emergency Center
hotlines.target: Milwaukee County residents of any age experiencing a mental health emergency
hotlines.notes: County-run crisis line staffed by counselors, therapists, psychologists and nurses that dispatches a non-police Mobile Crisis team; distinct from 988. Mental Health Emergency Center is a joint venture of Milwaukee County and the area's health systems.

hotlines.name: Sojourner Family Peace Center 24-Hour Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.organization: Sojourner Family Peace Center
hotlines.target: Domestic violence survivors in Milwaukee and outlying communities
hotlines.notes: Sojourner has been designated the 24-hour domestic violence hotline for the City of Milwaukee since 1986; distinct from the Wisconsin statewide domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: IMPACT 211 Milwaukee
hotlines.organization: IMPACT, Inc.
hotlines.target: Milwaukee-area residents seeking social-service referrals or crisis support
hotlines.notes: City of Milwaukee's designated 211 provider (operated by IMPACT, Inc.), confirmed via the city's own 211 page, with direct local/toll-free numbers distinct from the generic 211 dial code.

hotlines.name: Fulton County Behavioral Health Crisis Center
hotlines.organization: Fulton County Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities
hotlines.target: Fulton County residents experiencing a mental health crisis
hotlines.notes: County-run walk-in and call-in crisis center (opened 2024) operated with Grady Health System, offering peer support, observation chairs and crisis beds; distinct from the statewide Georgia Crisis & Access Line.

hotlines.name: Partnership Against Domestic Violence (PADV) Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: Partnership Against Domestic Violence
hotlines.target: Domestic violence survivors in Fulton and Gwinnett counties
hotlines.notes: PADV operates the only state-certified domestic violence safe houses in Fulton County and is listed as a primary crisis resource by the Fulton County Solicitor-General's office; distinct from Georgia's statewide domestic violence hotline.

hotlines.name: United Way of Greater Atlanta 211
hotlines.organization: United Way of Greater Atlanta
hotlines.target: Metro Atlanta residents, including Fulton County, seeking human-services referrals
hotlines.notes: Regional 211 contact center serving the 13-county Atlanta metro area including Fulton County, with a direct local number distinct from the generic 211 short code.

hotlines.name: Miami-Dade Mobile Response Team Crisis Line
hotlines.organization: WestCare/The Village South, contracted via Thriving Mind South Florida
hotlines.target: Miami-Dade County residents experiencing a behavioral health crisis who may need a mobile response
hotlines.notes: Mobile crisis response contracted specifically for Miami-Dade County by Thriving Mind South Florida, the state-designated managing entity for Miami-Dade and Monroe counties; distinct from the 988 Lifeline.

hotlines.name: Miami-Dade County Coordinated Victims Assistance Center
hotlines.organization: Miami-Dade County Community Action and Human Services Department (CAHSD)
hotlines.target: Domestic violence victims and their dependents in Miami-Dade County
hotlines.notes: County-run victim assistance hotline with a 24/7 text option added in 2020; distinct from Florida's statewide domestic violence hotline (1-800-500-1119).

hotlines.name: 211 Miami
hotlines.organization: 211 Miami (Switchboard of Miami), funded by The Children's Trust
hotlines.target: Miami-Dade County residents seeking crisis counseling and social-service referrals
hotlines.notes: Miami-Dade-specific crisis and information helpline funded by The Children's Trust, a dedicated Miami-Dade County revenue source created by voter referendum; direct-dial numbers distinct from the generic 211 short code.
